That escaping cluster is the same file set as 26f1ac7f8a6fec6d36465832dfb960b84a74ba1c, but APSB25-94 also fixes CVE-2025-54264 (second stored XSS) plus three authorization CVEs, and Adobe does not bind any hunk to CVE-2025-54266. Choosing one of these changes as the direct fix would be inference, not a first-party mapping. The finding is therefore not unpatched; the direct fix remains unidentified.

No atomic BIC object exists to inspect. Packaging authors (magento packaging service <magento-comops@adobe.com>) and the AC-14924 author (mohitradobe <cod33012@adobe.com>) cannot be used as BIC-local AI signals. Absence of Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailers on unrelated release snapshots is not an identity close.

findings: CVE-2025-54266 is a real, non-withdrawn Adobe CNA stored-XSS advisory (CWE-79, PR:H, UI:R) published 2025-10-14; GitHub withdrawn_at is not authoritative and the CVE.org state is PUBLISHED.

Vendor and GHSA sources give affected/fixed Magento Open Source release boundaries that resolve to exact tag objects in the assigned clone, but they never name the form field, persistence path, or rendering sink.
APSB25-94 simultaneously ships CVE-2025-54264, another stored XSS, so XSS-looking hunks in the October 2025 security releases are not uniquely attributable to this case.
Sibling packaging tags 2.4.6-p12/p13, 2.4.7-p7/p8, and 2.4.8-p2/p3 share parents and contain many unrelated changes; they are not atomic BICs or atomic direct fixes.

The only develop-line commit touching the p13 admin-button escaping files between 2.4.9-alpha2 and 2.4.9-alpha3 is 26f1ac7f8a6fec6d36465832dfb960b84a74ba1c (AC-14924, human Adobe author), a multi-file aggregate not labeled as CVE-2025-54266.

No first-party isolated patch, commit message, or researcher write-up maps CVE-2025-54266 to one hunk, so BIC search, parent-absence, squash decomposition, and BIC-only AI attribution remain unclosed. The required independent result is EVIDENCE_GAP, not FALSE_POSITIVE and not NOT_AI.
